claims.text: Adding about 3 vol.% Y2O3 nanoparticles to CoCrFeNi will promote formation and stabilization of a low-shear protective oxide tribofilm during sliding.
The Y2O3-modified alloy will maintain consistently low friction and wear from approximately 20 °C to 800 °C.
The starting oxide-free CoCrFeNi alloy has a conventional coarse-grained microstructure.
The coarse-grained starting microstructure causes higher friction and wear, especially at elevated temperatures.
Powder metallurgy and consolidated sintering can produce a nano-oxide-dispersion-strengthened CoCrFeNi microstructure containing about 3 vol.% Y2O3.
The Y2O3 particles will be evenly distributed in the CoCrFeNi matrix.
Dispersed Y2O3 particles will pin grain boundaries and refine or stabilize the alloy microstructure.
Y2O3 particles will serve as nucleation sites for a continuous, low-shear oxide tribolayer at high temperatures.
At low temperatures, Y2O3-induced grain refinement will maintain structural integrity by impeding grain-boundary sliding.
At elevated temperatures, Y2O3 particles will facilitate formation of a stable, lubricious oxide tribofilm.
The oxide tribofilm will reduce friction by lowering interfacial shear strength.
The oxide tribofilm will reduce wear by limiting direct metal-to-metal contact.
Relative to oxide-free CoCrFeNi, the modified alloy will reduce both coefficient of friction and wear rate by approximately 20–30% throughout 20–800 °C.
Conventional CoCrFeNi suffers increased friction and wear at high temperatures because of surface-film degradation and microstructural coarsening.
The proposed performance is bounded to sliding in ambient air, at laboratory-scale loads and speeds, between approximately 20 °C and 800 °C.
